headline: A 2022 law transfers specified federal land in Eunice, Louisiana to the city for free and shrinks the boundary of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve to match.
what_it_does: The Department of the Interior must give specified parcels of the original Eunice townsite to the city by quitclaim deed, with no payment required. A quitclaim deed transfers whatever interest the federal government holds without a promise about the land's condition or title. After the transfer, the park boundary is adjusted to leave out the conveyed land and other specified parcels in the original townsite.

who_it_affects.how: The city receives specified federal parcels in its original townsite at no cost.

who_it_affects.group: Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve
who_it_affects.how: The park's boundary is redrawn so the conveyed parcels and other specified townsite parcels are no longer part of the park.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors and residents near the original Eunice townsite
who_it_affects.how: Land that was in the federal park boundary becomes city-owned land, so federal park rules would no longer cover it.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on April 19, 2022. The summary does not give a separate deadline for the land transfer or the boundary change.
